The Work
 
The Director, Change Enablement advances EQ Bank’s enterprise Change Enablement practice, a standing capability within People & Talent accountable for readiness, adoption and sustained behaviour change across the Bank’s concurrent transformation agenda. The role closes the gap between funded transformation delivery and the employee readiness required to realize value across enterprise AI, PC Financial integration and convergence, and the EQB 2.0 operating model. Reporting to the Vice President, Talent, Transformation & Design, the incumbent owns the enterprise change method, demand prioritization, adoption readiness and executive-level visibility of change saturation. The mandate is to identify, plan, sequence and land change with the business, making adoption an engineered outcome rather than a communications task applied at go-live.  

The Core Responsibilities: Enterprise Change Enablement Strategy 
 Establish and maintain the enterprise Change Enablement practice within People & Talent, including standards, methods, tools, intake, demand prioritization and governance routines. 
 Own a tiered support model that sizes change enablement effort based on employee impact, adoption risk, complexity and strategic importance. 
 Maintain enterprise visibility of change saturation across major transformation programs and provide clear recommendations on sequencing, readiness and trade-offs. 
 Partner with program sponsors, business leaders, Enterprise AI, IMO, Convergence, EQB 2.0, Organization Design, Communications, Risk and Finance to ensure change, structure, process and value-realization plans are aligned. 
 Position adoption as a measurable business outcome by defining readiness criteria, adoption measures, sustainment practices and post-implementation review requirements. 
 Adoption, Readiness and Leader Enablement 
 Lead change impact assessments, stakeholder mapping, readiness assessments, resistance sensing and adoption planning for high-impact enterprise initiatives. 
 Design leader and manager enablement approaches that equip people leaders to communicate change with clarity, handle difficult questions and reinforce desired behaviours. 
 Create and maintain reusable change playbooks, templates, communications inputs, training supports and adoption measurement practices that can be scaled across initiatives. 
 Use employee feedback, pulse checks, readiness data, service data and adoption telemetry to identify friction early and adjust enablement plans. 
 Ensure change enablement aligns with EQB’s culture refresh, ways of working and employee experience commitments so transformation lands in a credible and consistent way. 
 Portfolio, Measurement and Executive Reporting 
 Maintain a consolidated enterprise change calendar across AI, integration, convergence and operating model initiatives to identify collisions, capacity pressure and sequencing risks. 
 Provide executive-level reporting on change saturation, readiness at go-live, adoption velocity, friction after go-live and time to value. 
 Translate readiness and adoption data into clear recommendations for senior leaders, including where to accelerate, pause, sequence differently or add support. 
 Partner with Finance value tracking teams to connect adoption and readiness to benefit realization, while maintaining clear accountability boundaries. 
 Partner with Risk, Compliance and control functions to ensure change plans meet regulatory expectations and produce evidence of readiness, adoption and sustainment where required. 
 Practice Governance and Flexible Capacity 
 Provide practice guidance, standards and coaching to partners applying change enablement methods across enterprise initiatives. 
 Build and manage a pre-qualified contractor pool to provide flexible capacity for large waves, peak demand, training build, communications production and adoption measurement. 
 Manage the Change Enablement operating budget, including contractor spend, and make pragmatic resourcing trade-offs across competing program demands. 
 Contribute to the broader People & Talent strategy and assess workforce upskilling and training needs arising from automation, role redesign and new ways of working.

 Strong judgement, resilience and credibility with senior leaders, including the ability to hold a view on sequencing, saturation and adoption risk when sponsors want to move faster. 
 Pragmatic self-starter who can operate strategically while also building templates, running workshops, writing briefing notes and solving practical implementation issues.
